tip: Indonesian often puts the object first: Tas kecil ini saya bawa = this small bag I'll take. The doer comes right after it, with no extra words needed.
tolong literally means help, and it turns any command into a polite request: Tolong taruh koper Anda = please put your suitcase.
baru means new, but before a verb it means only just or not until: penerbangan pengganti baru ada besok = the replacement flight isn't there until tomorrow.
English says you missed the plane; Indonesian says the plane left you behind: ketinggalan pesawat = got left behind by the plane.
sampai usually means until, but after a description it means so much that: berisik sekali sampai kami tidak bisa tidur = so noisy we couldn't sleep.
belum = not yet, and it's the negative for anything still pending: belum ada yang datang = no one has come yet. Tidak would state it flatly, as if no one will.
The everyday way to say per is se- (one): dua kali sehari = twice a day, literally two times one-day.
sama normally means same, but in everyday speech it also means with: sama keluarga = with family. Dengan is the formal version.
